old_caption: The video showcases a metallic spinner resting on a black rectangular base against a plain white background. The spinner consists of a central circular hub from which four cylindrical arms extend outward, each ending in a smaller cylindrical piece. The spinner rotates slowly and intermittently, with visible pauses and changes in orientation. As the spinner rotates, the arms and smaller pieces move in a circular motion, creating a display of motion and reflection. The consistent lighting highlights the shiny surfaces of the metallic parts, emphasizing their smooth texture and reflective properties. The video captures the intermittent spinning action without any significant changes in the environment or additional elements entering the frame.

caption: The video showcases a metallic four-arm spinner resting flat on a black rectangular pedestal against a plain white background. The spinner, built around a central ball-bearing ring with four cylindrical end weights joined by brass connector blocks, turns slowly about its vertical axis throughout the excerpt. A small dark notch on the bearing ring travels around its upper edge, marking the rotation. The arms drift between diagonal and more horizontal orientations relative to the stationary camera. As the body turns, the polished weights and gold blocks slide laterally and specular highlights shift across their curved surfaces. The object keeps its height and contact with the pedestal essentially constant, showing no onset, impact, or completion within the visible portion.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.

and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
